title: Rigveda 9.13: To Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 9.13: To Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 9.13 is a hymn of 9 verses addressed to Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 9, the hymns to Soma Pavamāna. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 673r-673v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 9.13.1-4 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 8, varga 1); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 673r
translation.original_text:
1soma̍ḥ punā̱no a̍rṣati sa̱hasra̍dhāro̱ atya̍viḥ | vā̱yor indra̍sya niṣkṛ̱tam ||
2pava̍mānam avasyavo̱ vipra̍m a̱bhi pra gā̍yata | su̱ṣvā̱ṇaṁ de̱vavī̍taye ||
3pava̍nte̱ vāja̍sātaye̱ somā̍ḥ sa̱hasra̍pājasaḥ | gṛ̱ṇā̱nā de̱vavī̍taye ||
4u̱ta no̱ vāja̍sātaye̱ pava̍sva bṛha̱tīr iṣa̍ḥ | dyu̱mad i̍ndo su̱vīrya̍m ||
translation.text:
1PASSED through, the fleece in thousand streams the Soma, purified, flows on To Indra's, Vâyu's special place.
2Sing forth, ye men who long for help, to Pavamâna, to the Sage, Effused to entertain the Gods.
3The Soma-drops with thousand powers are purified for victory, Hymned to become the feast of Gods.
4Yea, as thou flowest bring great store of food that we may win the spoil Indu, bring splendid manly might.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 673r (numbered 95r by the scribe) (OPenn image 673, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.13.1 ‹somaḥ punānaḥ arṣati sahasra-dhāraḥ›. Lines 1-6 carry hariḥ oṃ and the anukramaṇī for aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 8; 9.13.1 (somaḥ punānaḥ arṣati) begins in line 6 after oṃ. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 673v (numbered 95v by the scribe), begins in RV 9.13.5 ‹-sahasriṇam rayim pavantām ā›. Verses 9.13.1-4 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1somaḥ | punānaḥ | arṣati | sahasra-dhāraḥ | ati-aviḥ | vāyoḥ | indrasya | niḥ-kṛtam
2pavamānam | avasyavaḥ | vipram | abhi | pra | gāyata | suṣvāṇam | deva-vītaye
3pavante | vāja-sātaye | somāḥ | sahasra-pājasaḥ | gṛṇānāḥ | deva-vītaye
4uta | naḥ | vāja-sātaye | pavasva | bṛhatīḥ | iṣaḥ | dyu-mat | indo iti | su-vīryam

translation.original_ref: RV 9.13.5-9 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 8, varga 1); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 673v
translation.original_text:
5te na̍ḥ saha̱sriṇa̍ṁ ra̱yim pava̍ntā̱m ā su̱vīrya̍m | su̱vā̱nā de̱vāsa̱ inda̍vaḥ ||
6atyā̍ hiyā̱nā na he̱tṛbhi̱r asṛ̍gra̱ṁ vāja̍sātaye | vi vāra̱m avya̍m ā̱śava̍ḥ ||
7vā̱śrā a̍rṣa̱ntīnda̍vo̱ 'bhi va̱tsaṁ na dhe̱nava̍ḥ | da̱dha̱nvi̱re gabha̍styoḥ ||
8juṣṭa̱ indrā̍ya matsa̱raḥ pava̍māna̱ kani̍kradat | viśvā̱ apa̱ dviṣo̍ jahi ||
9a̱pa̱ghnanto̱ arā̍vṇa̱ḥ pava̍mānāḥ sva̱rdṛśa̍ḥ | yonā̍v ṛ̱tasya̍ sīdata ||
translation.text:
5May they in flowing give us wealth in thousands, and heroic power,– These Godlike Soma-drops effused.
6Like coursers by their drivers urged, they were poured forth, for victory, Swift through the woollen straining-cloth.
7Noisily flow the Soma-drops, like milch-kine lowing to their calves: They have run forth from both the hands.
8As Gladdener whom Indra loves, O Pavamâna, with a roar Drive all our enemies away.
9O Pavamamas, driving off the godless, looking on the light, Sit in the place of sacrifice.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 673v (numbered 95v by the scribe) (OPenn image 674, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.13.5 ‹-sahasriṇam rayim pavantām ā›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 674r (numbered 96r by the scribe), begins in RV 9.14.6 ‹ati śritī tiraścatā gavyā›. Verses 9.13.5-9 end on this page; 9.13.5 begins on fol. 673r (numbered 95r by the scribe).

5te | naḥ | sahasriṇam | rayim | pavantām | ā | su-vīryam | suvānāḥ | devāsaḥ | indavaḥ
6atyāḥ | hiyānāḥ | na | hetṛ-bhiḥ | asṛgram | vāja-sātaye | vi | vāram | avyam | āśavaḥ
7vāśrāḥ | arṣanti | indavaḥ | abhi | vatsam | na | dhenavaḥ | dadhanvire | gabhastyoḥ
8juṣṭaḥ | indrāya | matsaraḥ | pavamāna | kanikradat | viśvāḥ | apa | dviṣaḥ | jahi
9apa-ghnantaḥ | arāvṇaḥ | pavamānāḥ | svaḥ-dṛśaḥ | yonau | ṛtasya | sīdata
